required_quotations.quote: The correct analytical approach is to determine whether the termination provisions in an employment agreement read as a whole violate the ESA

definitions.ISSUE-01: Whether the termination clause is enforceable when the just-cause clause permits dismissal without notice for conduct short of the ESA wilful-misconduct standard, and whether a severability clause changes that.
definitions.ISSUE-02: How common-law reasonable notice is assessed and whether the discretionary bonus is recoverable during the notice period.
definitions.ISSUE-03: The statutory minimum entitlements: notice or pay in lieu, severance pay and its thresholds, and the wilful-misconduct exemption.
definitions.ISSUE-04: The minimum termination notice under Alberta's Employment Standards Code for the same employee.
definitions.PROP-01: Termination provisions are read as a whole; an illegal just-cause clause renders the without-cause clause unenforceable, and a severability clause is not applied to provisions that contract out of the ESA (Waksdale paras 10 and 14).
definitions.PROP-02: An employee's sophistication and access to independent legal advice do not override the plain language of a clause that contravenes the ESA (Rahman para 24).
definitions.PROP-03: The Court of Appeal has continued to apply Waksdale: Dufault v Ignace (Township), 2024 ONCA 915, para 24 (both clauses unenforceable; appeal dismissed para 27) and Wigdor v Facebook Canada Ltd., 2026 ONCA 572, para 62.
definitions.PROP-04: A dismissed employee recovers a lost bonus for the reasonable notice period unless the contract or plan unambiguously removes that right: the two questions in Matthews paras 52 and 55.
definitions.PROP-05: ESA s. 57 sets the minimum notice by length of employment; the employee here (eleven years) is entitled to eight weeks.
definitions.PROP-06: ESA s. 61 permits termination pay in a lump sum in lieu of notice.
definitions.PROP-07: ESA s. 64 severance pay requires five or more years' employment and an employer payroll of $2.5 million or more (or a mass termination).
definitions.PROP-08: O Reg 288/01 s. 2(1) para 3 exempts an employee guilty of wilful misconduct, disobedience or wilful neglect of duty that is not trivial and has not been condoned.
definitions.PROP-09: Alberta's Employment Standards Code s. 56 sets written termination notice by length of employment, eight weeks at ten years or more; s. 57 allows termination pay instead.
definitions.CONCLUSION-01: The termination clause is unenforceable and the employee is entitled to common-law reasonable notice.
definitions.CONCLUSION-02: The bonus is recoverable during the reasonable notice period unless the plan unambiguously takes that right away.
definitions.CLAIM-01: A severability clause preserves the without-cause termination clause when the just-cause clause violates the ESA.
definitions.CLAIM-02: The ESA minimum notice is the presumptive measure of common-law reasonable notice.
definitions.CLAIM-03: An employee's sophistication or access to legal advice validates a clause that contravenes the ESA.
definitions.CLAIM-04: Severance pay under s. 64 is owed regardless of the employer's payroll size or the employee's length of service.
